evals.expected_output: Treats the docstring as serving callers. Replaces the code-restating 'Gets the user' with information the signature does not already give: what `LookupError` means and when it occurs (not found vs backend failure), any constraints on `id`, and surprising behavior. Does not pad with multi-line restatement of the signature. Shows before/after.

evals.prompt: Write me a commit message for this change: I refactored the token buffer to use a fixed-size ring buffer instead of a `Vec`, so the lexer stops reallocating on every push during large files.
evals.expected_output: Produces a conventional commit with a concise imperative subject and a body that explains the why (eliminate per-push reallocation in the lexer hot path on large inputs) and the what (Vec to fixed-size ring buffer), serving the next person who blames the line. Leads with the point, no throat-clearing.

evals.prompt: Just review, don't rewrite: here's the intro paragraph of the README for our parser-combinator crate. 'This crate provides a comprehensive and flexible framework leveraging various combinatorial primitives to facilitate the construction of robust parsing solutions for a wide variety of input formats.' What's wrong with it?
evals.expected_output: Stays in review-only mode and reports problems in place rather than rewriting: buried lede (never says what the crate actually is or does concretely), empty intensifiers ('comprehensive', 'flexible', 'various', 'robust'), and jargon-as-marketing instead of a concrete example. Names what a good intro would lead with (show before explain) but does not produce the rewrite, since review was the deliverable.

evals.prompt: Help me rewrite this paragraph for our design doc (it's exposition, not a formal proof) explaining why our dataflow fixpoint iteration terminates: 'The algorithm keeps going over the lattice and applying the transfer functions until nothing changes, and because the lattice has finite height and the functions are monotone it has to stop eventually.'
evals.expected_output: Reads the mathematical-writing reference and preserves every claim (finite height, monotonicity, termination) exactly. Improves exposition: introduces the lattice and 'height' before relying on them, makes the termination argument explicit (monotone updates ascend a chain bounded by finite height), and prefers concrete phrasing over hand-waving — without turning it into a formal proof. Shows the revised text with a short note on what changed.

evals.prompt: Draft a PR description for a change that adds incremental recompilation to our build graph so unchanged modules are skipped on rebuild.
evals.expected_output: Writes for the reviewer audience: leads with what changed and why it matters (skip unchanged modules, faster rebuilds), summarizes the approach at the right altitude, and notes risk/verification (how correctness of skipping is ensured). Structured and scannable, point first, no buried lede.
